_schema._about: Topographia Sacra · canonical gazetteer across all books in the series. Each entry is a place named in scripture, keyed by a stable lowercase slug. Edit this file to revise identifications across the whole series; chapter pages read from it at load.

fields.name: Display name (English form, as used by Anchor Bible Dictionary)
fields.name_alt: Alternative names or transliterations, optional, for search/index
fields.coords: [latitude, longitude] of the leading identification, decimal degrees, WGS84
fields.alternatives: Optional array of {site, source} for disputed identifications; cite footnote in chapter data
fields.appearances: Array of {book, chapter, verses} where the place is named

tier_meanings.conjectural: Best guess, multiple candidates, or general region only
tier_meanings.unknown: Named but unlocatable; should NOT appear on a map — list only in gazetteer

jericho.name: Jericho
jericho.id: Tell es-Sultan, on the western edge of the Jordan Valley c. 10 km NW of the Dead Sea. Excavated by Sellin & Watzinger, Garstang, Kenyon, and most recently by the Italian–Palestinian expedition.

gilgal.name: Gilgal
gilgal.id: Israelite encampment east of Jericho near the Jordan. Several candidates have been proposed in the plain between Tell es-Sultan and the river; no site has produced decisive evidence.

jordan.name: The Jordan
jordan.id: The Jordan River; the crossing point in the Joshua narrative is traditionally placed opposite Jericho near the el-Maghtas ford, modern Qasr el-Yahud.

ai.name: Ai
ai.id: A fortified site east of Bethel in the central hill country. The traditional identification is et-Tell ("the mound"), excavated by Marquet-Krause and Callaway, but the site shows no Late Bronze occupation, prompting alternative proposals.

alternatives.source: Albright; Callaway (traditional consensus, but stratigraphy problematic)
Bryant Wood / Associates for Biblical Research

bethel.name: Bethel
bethel.id: Beitin, a village c. 17 km north of Jerusalem on the central ridge route. Identified by Edward Robinson (1838) and excavated by Albright and Kelso. Earlier called Luz (Joshua 18:13).

beth-aven.name: Beth-aven
beth-aven.id: A site "east of Bethel" in the Joshua narrative, used as a directional landmark. Possibly identical with later Beth-el itself (so Hosea 4:15) or a now-lost site between Bethel and Ai. No archaeological identification has been confirmed.

shebarim.name: Shebarim
shebarim.id: Mentioned only as the place to which Israel was pursued from Ai (Joshua 7:5). The Hebrew may be a common noun ("the quarries" or "the shattered places") rather than a place name; if a place, it is unlocated.

valley-of-achor.name: Valley of Achor
valley-of-achor.id: A wadi on the route between Jericho and the central hill country, named for the "trouble" (Hebrew 'akar) caused by Achan. Most often identified with the Wadi Qelt or the Buqei'ah valley west of Jericho; the precise location is debated.

shittim.name: Shittim
shittim.id: The Israelite encampment in the plains of Moab east of the Jordan, c. 12 km ENE of Jericho. No site has been archaeologically confirmed; the leading candidates are Tell el-Hammam and Tell el-Kefrein, both on the well-watered plain north of the Dead Sea.

adam.name: Adam
adam.id: Tell ed-Damiyeh, on the east bank of the Jordan near the mouth of the Jabbok, c. 25 km north of Jericho. The identification is secure on linguistic and topographic grounds; the site sits at a constriction in the Jordan corridor where landslide damming of the river has been historically attested.

zarethan.name: Zarethan
zarethan.id: An unconfirmed site in the Jordan Valley, named here as the city beside Adam. The leading candidate is Tell es-Saʿidiyeh, c. 28 km north of Jericho on the east bank; Tell Umm Hamad has also been proposed.

dead-sea.name: The Dead Sea
dead-sea.id: The salt lake at the southern end of the Jordan Rift Valley, c. 80 km long, the lowest point on the earth's surface (−430 m). Called the “Salt Sea” and the “sea of the Arabah” in the Hebrew Bible. Forms the eastern boundary of Judah and the western boundary of Moab.

mount-ebal.name: Mount Ebal
mount-ebal.id: The northern of the two mountains flanking Shechem (modern Nablus), 940 m above sea level. Site of Joshua's altar and the inscription of the law in the MT, LXX, and Vulgate; the Samaritan Pentateuch and 4QJosh^a place the altar on Mount Gerizim instead.

mount-gerizim.name: Mount Gerizim
mount-gerizim.id: The southern of the two mountains flanking Shechem (modern Nablus), 881 m above sea level. The Samaritan holy mountain, site of a Samaritan temple from the Persian period; the Samaritan Pentateuch's reading of Deuteronomy 27:4 places Joshua's altar here rather than on Mount Ebal.

gibeon.name: Gibeon
gibeon.id: el-Jib, c. 9 km NW of Jerusalem on the central ridge route. Identified by Edward Robinson (1838); Pritchard's excavations later recovered jar handles inscribed gbʿn (Gibeon), confirming the identification beyond reasonable doubt.

chephirah.name: Chephirah
chephirah.id: Khirbet el-Kefira (also Kefireh), c. 11 km W of Jerusalem on a ridge above the Wadi Qatrun. One of the four Hivite/Gibeonite cities. Iron Age occupation has been confirmed by survey.

beeroth.name: Beeroth
beeroth.id: Identification disputed. The traditional candidate is el-Bireh, just N of Ramallah; alternatives include Khirbet el-Burj near Tell el-Ful and Nebi Samwil.

kiriath-jearim.name: Kiriath Jearim
kiriath-jearim.id: Tell el-Azhar (Deir el-Azhar), c. 13 km W of Jerusalem on the central ridge route. Identified by Robinson and confirmed by excavation; the Iron Age site sits directly atop a Bronze Age tell.

jerusalem.name: Jerusalem
jerusalem.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

hebron.name: Hebron
hebron.id: Tel Rumeida (within modern Hebron / al-Khalil), in the Judean hill country c. 30 km SSW of Jerusalem. The patriarchal city of the Cave of Machpelah; king Hoham named here as a southern coalition member.

jarmuth.name: Jarmuth
jarmuth.id: Tel Yarmut (Khirbet Yarmuk), in the Shephelah c. 25 km W of Jerusalem. A major Early Bronze and Late Bronze fortified site, identified by Robinson and confirmed by recent excavations.

lachish.name: Lachish
lachish.id: Tel Lachish (Tell ed-Duweir), the largest mound in the Shephelah, c. 40 km SW of Jerusalem. Identified by Albright; thoroughly excavated. The Late Bronze destruction layer (Stratum VII / VI) sits awkwardly with the conquest narrative — see footnote.

eglon.name: Eglon
eglon.id: Identification disputed. Tell el-Hesi (Petrie/Bliss) was the older candidate; Tell Aitun / Khirbet ʿAjlan, c. 8 km W of Lachish, is now generally favored. The pin marks Tell Aitun.

beth-horon.name: Beth Horon
beth-horon.id: Two villages on the ascent from the Aijalon Valley to the central hill country: Upper Beth Horon (Beit ʿUr al-Foqa, 617 m) and Lower Beth Horon (Beit ʿUr al-Tahta, 400 m), c. 2 km apart. The pin marks the upper village; the “ascent of Beth Horon” is the road between them.

azekah.name: Azekah
azekah.id: Tell Zakariyeh, in the Shephelah overlooking the Elah Valley, c. 25 km SW of Jerusalem. A prominent fortified site through the Iron Age; identified by Robinson.

makkedah.name: Makkedah
makkedah.id: Identification disputed. Khirbet el-Qom (c. 13 km W of Hebron) and Khirbet Beit Maqdum have both been proposed. The pin marks Khirbet el-Qom.

valley-of-aijalon.name: The Valley of Aijalon
valley-of-aijalon.id: The broad valley running east-west between the central ridge and the Shephelah, named for the village of Aijalon (modern Yalo). The natural corridor from the coastal plain to the hill country, the valley is the locus of v.12’s “Sun, stand still on Gibeon; you, moon, in the valley of Aijalon.”

libnah.name: Libnah
libnah.id: Identification disputed. Tel Burna (Tell Bornat) in the Shephelah is the leading current candidate; Tell es-Safi was earlier proposed but has now been identified as Gath, removing it from contention.

alternatives.source: older proposals — now identified as Gath

gezer.name: Gezer
gezer.id: Tel Gezer, on the northern edge of the Shephelah c. 30 km W of Jerusalem. A major Bronze and Iron Age site; the identification was secured by inscribed boundary stones recovered by Macalister.

debir.name: Debir
debir.id: Khirbet Rabud, in the southern Judean hill country c. 12 km SW of Hebron. Identified by Kochavi against the older Albright proposal of Tell Beit Mirsim, which lacked the necessary water source and Late Bronze occupation profile.

kadesh-barnea.name: Kadesh Barnea
kadesh-barnea.id: ʿAin Qudeirat, the largest spring in the northern Sinai / Negev frontier, c. 80 km SW of Beersheba. The Israelite encampment of Numbers 13–14 and the southernmost reach of the conquest in v.41.

gaza.name: Gaza
gaza.id: The southernmost of the five Philistine pentapolis cities, on the coastal plain c. 80 km SW of Jerusalem. The west-coast extreme of the southern campaign’s reach in v.41.

goshen-of-judah.name: Goshen (of Judah)
goshen-of-judah.id: Distinct from the Egyptian Goshen of Genesis–Exodus. A region in the southern Shephelah / Judean foothills, sometimes identified with the area around Tell el-Khuweilfeh; precise extent unknown.
